# World map fixture (Minecraft 26.3)

The golden fixture of the world map renderer (v1.4; the spec is [docs/reference.md "World map"](../../../docs/reference.md#world-map)).
`tests/test_map_reference.py` renders it with the Python reference renderer (`tests/map_reference.py`) and checks
every tile against `golden.json`; the Rust renderer must produce byte-identical tiles (same paths, same sha256,
`rendered_at` 0).

## Contents (942 KB)

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `dimensions/minecraft/overworld/region/r.{0.-1,0.0,0.1,1.0,1.1}.mca` | 50 `minecraft:full` chunks in two 5 x 5 patches: chunks x 4..8, z -4..0 (forest, beach, ocean, snow) and x 29..33, z 29..33 (crossing the corner of four regions, so north-neighbour shading crosses region borders); plus one chunk of each other status per region (`structure_starts`, `biomes`, `terrain`, `initialize_light`), which the renderer skips |
| `dimensions/minecraft/the_end/region/r.0.0.mca` | 1 full chunk (0, 0), the main island's centre, plus one chunk of each other status |
| `dimensions/smallworld/synthetic/region/` | generated edge cases (`scripts/map_fixture.py synthetic`): see-through blocks, water depths 1..16, waterlogged stairs and slabs, lava, colour ties, slopes, bedrock/void columns, glass down to the bottom of the world, a 300-entry palette, mixed string/compound palettes with missing properties, gzip / none / external `.mcc` chunks, and chunks to skip (provisional status, another DataVersion, a chunk in the wrong slot) |
| `golden.json` | sha256 of every tile, the palette's sha256 and the render summary |

## Where the real chunks come from

A world generated by the pinned server (Purpur 26.3 build 2655, DataVersion 5023) with `level-seed=12345` and
default settings, during the v1.4 design: the server ran briefly with no player ever joining, so only two small
patches were generated in full. It is sparse: only about 50 chunks in the whole world are `full`
(Paper saves many proto-chunks), so the fixture keeps the regions with full chunks and nothing else.

The chunks are copied byte for byte (compressed payload and region timestamp as the server wrote them). Nothing
else is: no `level.dat` (the renderer takes the dimension's minimum Y from each chunk's `yPos`), no `players/`,
no `entities/`, no `poi/`, no `data/`. `map_fixture.py trim` refuses a chunk with anything that could identify a
player or an entity (UUIDs, names, owners, sign or book text, player-head profiles, entities). The block
entities left are generated structures' (chests, spawners, sculk, an ancient city's skull without a profile).

## Regenerating it (on a Minecraft version bump)

1. Regenerate the palette for the new version: `python scripts/map_palette.py dump`.
2. Generate a fresh world with the new pinned server and `level-seed=12345` on a throwaway machine or CI runner
   (the product never runs the server on a developer's machine; `scripts/boot_test.py` shows the settings),
   ideally with a few `/forceload add` patches (one crossing a region corner) so there are full chunks.
3. `python scripts/map_fixture.py trim <world> --out tests/fixtures/world-<version>` (the real chunks),
   `python scripts/map_fixture.py synthetic --out tests/fixtures/world-<version>` (the edge cases).
4. Point `FIXTURE` in `tests/map_reference.py` at the new directory, run `python tests/map_reference.py golden`,
   look at a few tiles (`python scripts/map_preview.py --world tests/fixtures/world-<version> --zoom 2 out.png`),
   and delete the old fixture.
